Legum statuta swadent et necessarium est, vt acta hominum que aguntur, ne ubliuio sit solita ea recesare a memoria, debeant ydoneorum virorum testibus nec non litterarum apicibus solidan. Nos igitur Heinricus de Rosenberch et Zmilo de Gretzen ad vniuer- sorum noticiam presenti scripto tam presentium quam futurorum in ueri deposicione testimonii cupimus peruenire, quod reuerendus dominus Otto abbas de Hobenfurt pariter et totus conuentus fratrum eiusdem monasterii emerunt vniuersa bona in Horzitz cum om nibus ad hec pertinenciis pratis rubetis cultis et incultis apud viros nobiles dominum Zawissium et dominum Witigonem fratres de Laedenitz empcionis more racionabili ac consueto , que quondam viri nobilis domini Heinrici de Cozzowahora fuerunt ex ipsius uolun- tate gratuita omnimodo et consensu, qui eciam coram magnificencia illustri regis Boemie Wenzeslay nunc regnantis pro se atque pueris suis ipsa bona estuantibus desideriis animoque discretiuo affectuosius resignauit dicto domino abbati atque conuentui fratrum dicti monas terii, prout priuilegia dicti regis incliti lucidius protestantur. Porro auctor sceleris, perswasor fraudis, leo rugiens, milleartifexseminator zizanie, suum lolium seminauit, ita ut ipsius pueri dicti domini Hein rici de Cozzowahora ipsum dominum abbatem bonis inpeterent pro eisdem. Ad decidendam autem cuiuslibet materiam scandali seu omnis omnino inconuenientem incongruamque causam litigi i dictorum puerorum medullitus abolendam ab utraque parte scilicet a domino abbate a dictis pueris peremptorie in arbitros eligebamur. Huic honeri tanquam illi, qui virtutem colimus, vicium profligamus, no- stros humeros submittentes pactibus interclusis, si prefatus dominus abbas nostro arbitrio non obediret, quod foret ïn quingentis marcis argentis nobis arhitris obligatus, et si uice uersa prenominati pueri ausu temerario sen moti maliuolencia qualicumque nostro arbitrio in aliquo contrairent, quod similiter nobis arbitris quingentas marcas 86 argenti persoluerent quolibet dubii sine scrupulo. Huius autem per- solucionis totidem marcarum videlicet quingentarum dominus Bern- hardus de Bernhartitz ex parte dictorum puerorum uersus nos est in solidum perpetuus fideiussor. entries.english:
1293, 15 June, Prague. — Bishop Theodoric of Olomouc grants indulgences to the Cistercian monastery at Hohenfurt. On the same day and at the same place, Bishops Heinrich of Merseburg and Bernard of Meissen also grant indulgences to the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Hohenfurt.

L. Theodoric, by the grace of God Bishop of Olomouc, to all the faithful of Christ to whom these presents come, greetings in the Lord Jesus Christ. Since a branch of good works has no greenness unless it remains in the root of charity, we urge the devotion of all of you in the Lord and ask you to give pious alms, from the goods bestowed on you by God, to the monastery of Saint Mary, Mother of God, at Hohenfurt in the Diocese of Prague, for the love of Jesus Christ, purchasing eternal life with things transitory. Trusting in the mercy of almighty God and the patronage of his most beloved Mother, we mercifully grant in the Lord forty days’ remission of the penance imposed on all who are truly penitent and have confessed, who extend helping hands to the aforesaid monastery, and who visit it out of devotion to seek forgiveness for their sins. These presents shall remain valid in perpetuity.

Given at Prague in the year of the Lord 1293, on the feast of Saint Vitus.

Seal: A well-preserved white-wax seal hanging from a parchment strip, showing a bishop standing and blessing. The legend reads: “Theodoric, by the grace of God, Bishop of Olomouc.”

1293, 15 June, Prague. — Bishops Heinrich of Merseburg and Bernard of Meissen likewise grant indulgences to the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Hohenfurt.

Heinrich, Bishop of Merseburg, and Bernard, Bishop of Meissen, by the grace of God, to all to whom this document comes, greetings in the Lord. Since, by virtue of the sacred episcopal office entrusted to us by divine dispensation, we are bound to invite the faithful of Christ to works of piety and to render due honor to God and his holy churches by means of indulgences and remissions, so that they may thereby become more ready to merit divine grace, we mercifully grant, from the mercy of almighty God, forty days’ remission of the penances imposed on all who are truly penitent and have confessed and who, in a humble spirit of devotion, visit the monastery at Hohenfurt, of the Cistercian Order in the Diocese of Prague, on the four feasts of the glorious Virgin Mary, on the feasts of the Nativity of the Lord, the Resurrection, and Pentecost, or during each of the octaves of those feasts; or who lovingly extend helping hands toward the construction of that monastery, its lamps, ornaments, or other needs. This grant is conditional on the consent of the diocesan bishop of that place. These presents shall remain valid in perpetuity.

Given at Prague in the year of the Lord 1293, on the feast of the martyr Saint Vitus. The episcopate of Merseburg was in its eleventh year, and that of Meissen in its first.

Seal: Bernard of Meissen’s seal is missing. The other seal is somewhat damaged, in white wax, hanging from a parchment strip; it shows a bishop seated on a chair. The surviving legend reads in part: “Seal of Heinrich, by the grace of God, Bishop of the Church of Merseburg.”

1293, 12 July, Zobizlaus. — Heinrich von Rosenberg and Smil von Gratzen, acting as arbitrators, amicably settle the dispute between Hohenfurt Abbey and the sons of Heinrich von Kossowa Hora concerning the estates at Hořice.

The statutes of the law urge, and it is necessary, that human acts be made firm by the testimony of suitable men and by written records, lest they be erased from memory by the customary passage of time. Therefore, we, Heinrich von Rosenberg and Smil von Gratzen, wish by this present writing to make known to all, now and in the future, as true testimony, that the reverend Lord Otto, abbot of Hohenfurt, and the entire convent of that monastery bought all the estates at Hořice, with all their appurtenances, meadows, brushland, cultivated and uncultivated land, from the noble lords Zawissius and Witigo, brothers of Ledenice, by a reasonable and customary purchase. These estates had formerly belonged to the noble Lord Heinrich of Kossowa Hora, who, by his free will and full consent, had relinquished them to the aforesaid abbot and convent for himself and his children, moved by a fervent desire and a discerning purpose, before the illustrious majesty of the currently reigning King Wenceslas of Bohemia, as the privileges of that renowned king more fully attest.

But the author of crime, persuader of deceit, roaring lion, master of a thousand tricks, and sower of discord planted his tares, so that the aforesaid Lord Heinrich’s sons brought a claim against the abbot over those estates. To settle every cause of scandal and thoroughly put an end to all improper and unfitting litigation by those sons, both parties—the abbot and the said sons—chose us as arbitrators by formal appointment. We undertook this burden, as men who cultivate virtue and drive out vice, under the following conditions: if the aforesaid abbot failed to obey our award, he would owe us, the arbitrators, 500 marks of silver; and if, conversely, the aforesaid sons opposed our award in any respect, whether rashly or from any ill will, they would likewise pay us 500 marks of silver, without any possible dispute. Lord Bernhard von Bernhartitz, on behalf of the sons, is their joint and perpetual surety for payment of that same sum of 500 marks.

In our arbitration we decreed—although the religious men were under no legal obligation to pay anything—that they should give the aforesaid sons 50 marks of silver, so that from then on the sons would no longer harass the abbot and his brethren with claims concerning those same estates at Hořice, but would possess them peacefully and freely, by hereditary right and in perpetuity, with every objection removed. They have duly carried this out according to our award, paying the aforesaid sons the full 50 marks of silver. This arbitration was made effective in the presence of the noble lords Zezema of Landstein, Wok von Witigau, and Hoger of Lomnice, and was firmly confirmed.

To preserve this clear confirmation, unimpaired and unbroken for all time, we have had the present letters written for the aforesaid abbot and convent of Hohenfurt as evident testimony and protection, authenticated by our seals and by the seals of the noblemen in whose presence the above arbitration was made. The witnesses listed below are: Lord Stephan of Přesnitz; Lord Nedamir of Lobenitz; Lord Ontscho of Nemschitz; Lord Liupold of Vgetz, knights of Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg; Wltsch of Zedlo; Albert and Budylo, brothers called of Horach; Lord Hron and Lord Dytmar, brothers of Zbinitz, knights of Lord Smil of Gratzen; Lord Ztata of Vdin, knight of Lord Hoger of Lomnice; Lord Lutebor of Zletowitz; and many other sensible and prudent men.

These acts took place at Zobizlaus in the year of the Lord 1293, on 12 July.

Seals: Five white-wax seals hanging from parchment strips. The first is a small triangular seal with a five-petaled rose, bearing the legend “Seal of Wok of Witigau”; the second is a very small triangular seal with the same rose, bearing the legend “Seal of Smil of Gratzen”; the third is Heinrich von Rosenberg’s equestrian seal, damaged here (see no. XXXIII); the fourth is a round seal with a triangular shield bearing a five-petaled rose, the seal of Hoger of Lomnice; the fifth is a very small round seal showing a helmet with a rose, of which only three petals remain, each petal-tip itself displaying a five-petaled rose. Millauer, p. 113, no. 27.
